description: Pixi.js v8 framework layer — async Application init, rotating gradient badge, resize + HMR dispose wired from first render.

buildHints.whenToUse: High-performance 2D canvas work — interactive data viz, particle systems, generative art, map editors, live charts. Pick over Phaser when you want a raw renderer without scene+physics machinery.
firstSteps: Run `pnpm install` then `pnpm dev` — Vite serves on 5173 with HMR; a rotating gradient badge renders immediately.
Pixi v8 uses `await app.init(...)` — it is ASYNC. Do not call `new Application()` and start rendering synchronously; sprites attached before init never appear.
Put art in `public/assets/` and load via `Assets.load('assets/foo.png')` — the v8 Assets loader replaces the v7 Loader class.
Attach children to `app.stage` (or a sub-Container). `app.ticker.add(...)` drives per-frame updates.
Run `pnpm build` to emit static assets to `dist/` — deploy on any static host.
gotchas: Pixi v8 is a BREAKING rewrite of v7. Do NOT copy v7 tutorials — `new Application({ width, height })` is gone; use `const app = new Application(); await app.init({ width, height });`.
Pixi v8 supports both WebGL and WebGPU. Default renderer is chosen automatically — pin with `preference: 'webgpu'` if needed.
The Ticker runs after `app.init()` only. Don't add ticker callbacks before init — they're attached to a placeholder and never fire.
On teardown (HMR, route change), call `app.destroy(true, { children: true, texture: true })` to release GPU memory. Without it, HMR leaks textures fast.
`import.meta.hot` requires Vite client types — `src/vite-env.d.ts` provides the reference directive; do not delete it or typecheck will fail on the HMR block.
architectureNotes: Application owns: renderer, stage (root Container), ticker. One Application per canvas.
Scene composition = Container hierarchy. Containers transform children; leaves are Sprites, Graphics, Text, Mesh.
